en: The Great Staff Dhāraṇī, the Cool One. [0] [Siddham] Homage to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas! [1] Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling in Rājagṛha.
In the great cremation ground of Śītavana, in the vicinity of the Iṅghikāyātana,
the Venerable Rāhula was being excessively tormented there by celestial seizers, nāga seizers, yakṣa seizers, rākṣasa seizers,
kinnara seizers, garuḍa seizers, mahoraga seizers, human seizers, non-human seizers, and preta seizers.
[He was surrounded] by elemental spirits, by piśāca spirits, by kumbhāṇḍa spirits, by leopards, crows, owls, insects, reptiles, and other beings, both human and non-human.
Then the Venerable Rāhula approached the place where the Blessed One was; having approached, he [touched] the feet of the Blessed One.
Having prostrated with his head at the feet of the Blessed One and circumambulated him three times, he stood before the Blessed One weeping, shedding tears.
Then the Blessed One, though already knowing this, addressed Rāhula:
"Rāhula, why do you stand before me shedding tears?"
When this had been said, the Venerable Rāhula addressed the Blessed One as follows:
"Here, Blessed One, I am dwelling at Rājagṛha, in the Cool Grove, in the Great Cemetery, at the site of the Iṅghikāyātana."
Thus, Blessed One, I was harassed there by divine seizers, naga seizers, yakṣa seizers, rākṣasa seizers,
kinnara seizers, garuḍa seizers, mahoraga seizers, human seizers, non-human seizers, preta seizers, bhūta seizers,
piśāca seizers, kumbhāṇḍa seizers, as well as by leopards, crows, owls, insects, and reptiles.
"And by other beings, both human and non-human.
Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Rāhula:
"Rāhula, you must take up this great *daṇḍadhāraṇī* spell."

It will serve for the protection, defense, and guardianship of the fourfold assembly—of monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen—and will lead to their welfare, benefit, and happiness for a long time. Namely: Aṅgas, Vaṅgas.

May they grant protection for me and for all sentient beings;

[7] Indeed, Rāhula, when this *Mahādaṇḍadhāraṇī* vidyā— having tied a knot in a sūtra consisting of at least one hundred and eight words— is worn on the hand or worn around the neck, protection will be established for a full hundred yojanas in every direction.
Neither by means of perfumes, flowers, nor mudrās will any human or non-human prevail over him;
neither poison, nor weapons, nor disease, nor fever, nor high fever, nor spells and mantras, nor vetālas;
neither by illness, nor by fire, nor by poison or water will he meet his end.
It binds all applications of spells and mantras when properly employed;
it liberates those who are bound by others;
and it brings about the destruction of all diseases, sorrows, and obstacles.
It pacifies the defilements of the Kali age;
it liberates one from all planetary seizures.
Whatever seizure [a spirit] may not release—
His head shall split into seven pieces like the cluster of blossoms on an arjaka tree.
And Vajrapāṇi, the great general of the yakṣas, having meditated with his vajra—blazing, fiercely flaming, and become a single mass of fire—shall shatter his head.
Furthermore, the four Great Kings shall destroy him with an iron wheel, striking with the edge of a razor.
Therefore, there shall be a falling away from that world of yakṣas,
and one does not find residence in the capital city of Aḍakavatī.

Indeed, Rāhula, when this Great Daṇḍadhāraṇī spell has been recited even once, one who is situated in the midst of kings, thieves, water, fire, poison, weapons, forests, wildernesses, or mountain passes shall be freed from all fears.
It is liberated.

Indeed, this Great Staff Dhāraṇī-vidyā has been spoken, is being spoken, and will be spoken by Buddhas as numerous as the sands of ninety-one Ganges rivers; it is accomplished, supremely accomplished, and [honored] by all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas.
She is worshipped, surrounded by a multitude of all people;
may there be auspiciousness and health for me and for all sentient beings amidst all fears and calamities.
Thus spoke the Blessed One; and the Venerable Rāhula, being uplifted, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.
[10] The Noble Mahādaṇḍadhāraṇī Śītavatī is completed.
